summary: Independent review of the updated Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 c23694172c96fe9942c09c7b0bdb542e0018da3c037a022cd391b43638b35701. All 28 packaged files byte-match source. Grouping uses allowlisted fields, stable nested keys, preserved leaf ordering, and explicit missing/completion-band handling. Expand controls are placed before row content. The previously identified bulk-nudge scope and recipient races are fixed: nested actions use exact group member IDs, global actions include saved selected-release IDs even without cached rows, and copy/open binds the original recipient URL and aborts navigation after a drawer or recipient change. Fresh batched GUS reads retain all requested references or fail closed; current lead IDs distinguish same-name recipients. Slack output is escaped and no sending API exists. Independently executed all 19 focused controls, grouping, and nudge tests successfully. No blocking issues remain. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment. The clipboard-rejection path now checks the original drawer and editor existence before selecting text, resolving the previously noted closed-drawer error race. The final group-by trigger uses a compact selection count while full labels remain in options and group headers; the text remains assigned through textContent.
caveats: Slack actions prepare and copy reminders and optionally open a verified workspace-qualified DM. They do not send messages or prefill a Slack draft. Native mention recognition and pasted formatting require user verification in Slack before manual sending.

Actual Slack identity lookup, workspace deep-link navigation, and native Slack paste were not verified; browser identities and clipboard flows were mocked. Missing identity/workspace capabilities produce copy-only guidance.

Bulk preparation is limited to 500 epics and rejects oversized messages rather than omitting references. Missing-only selection reflects the fresh planning snapshot; later changes can require replanning.

Existing strict heuristic AI grounding/fallback, chronological rich-text fail-closed behavior, usage completeness, preview cache/cancellation, refresh concurrency, journal growth, revision conflicts, non-atomic updates, preference semantics, host/catalog/history limits, and AllUsers sharing caveats remain.
Current GUS Apps host metadata still relies on verified-definition snapshots; future automatic list-column detection remains unavailable without live list-view REST capability.

This review combined static source/artifact inspection with 19 independently executed focused tests. The implementing agent reported all 163 Node tests and GA-controls, group-nudge, compact-epic, and monthly-AI browser suites passed. Additional race/scope regression tests were being added without artifact changes; these broader suites, production-host/model behavior, remote publication, and golden-tag movement were not independently verified.
